1) Role clarity — Aurelia requires an explicit Processor/Controller delegation matrix in the DPA.
2) Cross-border transfers — preference for EU-resident processing; if not feasible, SCCs + documented TIA with remedial controls.
3) Subprocessor visibility — a monthly notice and right to object within 15 days.

Ben — quick read and high-level positions below. I've attached a tracked-response doc.

Summary (high-level):
- Role matrix: Redwood is the Processor for SaaS inference and logging features; we can accept a clarified Exhibit A / Roles table that reflects this. We will not accept language that makes Redwood a Controller for customer data.
- SCCs: we can execute the latest EU Commission SCCs; need procurement to confirm which SCC module (controller-processor) they expect.
- Data localization: we can offer EU-region-only processing for production workloads where contractually required (depends on Dedicated vs Hosted). For hosted customers we can commit to EU-region routing and a contractual statement of primary processing location.
- TIA: Security will produce a short TIA summary that references encryption in transit & at rest, key management, and subprocessors. If they insist on a formal TIA report, that will be a paid engagement — we can offer a standard Redwood TIA summary free of charge.
- Subprocessors: we accept monthly notice + 15-day objection; exceptions for critical infra changes.

Open items for negotiation (we recommend counter proposals):
1) Limit audit rights to on-site audits by mutual agreement / or remote evidence review to reduce operational burden.
2) Narrow indemnity / liability language tied to data breaches caused by Redwood's negligence only.
3) Clarify export controls / law enforcement request handling (we can add a Law Enforcement Requests subsection).

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Response_trackchanges.docx (docx) — contains tracked language. TIA_Summary.xlsx — short control mapping. Redlines noted inline with recommended counters.

Proposed internal ETA: we can produce the response and an internal TIA summary by Monday 2025-06-09. If Aurelia needs faster turnaround we can accelerate but would like confirmation of which items are deal-breakers.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Laura / team — thanks for the quick read. A few clarifications from ours:

- Module: Aurelia expects the Controller-Processor SCC module.
- EU processing: production data must be processed in EU regions for PHI-derived datasets; test/staging can be in US if adequately isolated.
- TIA: the free TIA summary is fine to start; Procurement may request a deeper report later.

Timeline request: procurement is aiming for signature by 2025-06-23. Can Redwood commit to final language and a DocuSign-ready package by 2025-06-16? If not, please propose a target.

Also: please confirm whether Redwood can provide a list of subprocessors and whether the notice cadence can be monthly via email (not portal).

Emma
